q: In a (noncontracting) context-sensitive grammar, every production α → β satisfies…
explain: Rules never shorten the sentential form. (S → ε is allowed as a special case, if S never appears on a right-hand side.)

q: In the Chomsky hierarchy, context-sensitive grammars are…
explain: Type 0 is unrestricted, type 1 context-sensitive, type 2 context-free and type 3 regular.

q: Which language is context-sensitive but not context-free?
explain: aⁿbⁿcⁿ fails the CFL pumping lemma, but a noncontracting grammar with rules like CB → BC generates it. The others are already context-free.

q: In the grammar for aⁿbⁿcⁿ (S → aSBC | aBC, CB → BC, aB → ab, bB → bb, bC → bc, cC → cc), what does the rule CB → BC do?
options: Moves B's in front of C's, so they can be sorted
Starts a new block of a's
explain: S lays down a's followed by interleaved B and C. CB → BC swaps them until all the B's come first. Only then can the terminal-making rules finish.

q: Membership (is w ∈ L(G)?) is decidable for every context-sensitive grammar G.
explain: True. Since no rule shrinks the string, every sentential form on the way to w has length ≤ |w|. There are finitely many of those, so a search always terminates.

q: Which rule is not allowed in a context-sensitive grammar?
explain: AB → A shrinks the string from length 2 to length 1. The others keep or increase the length.

q: Which machine model accepts exactly the context-sensitive languages?
options: The Turing machine with unlimited tape
explain: An LBA is a nondeterministic Turing machine restricted to the part of the tape holding its input. Topic 20 covers it in detail.

q: Every context-free language that does not contain ε is context-sensitive.
explain: True. A CNF grammar has rules A → BC and A → a, which never shrink the string, so it is already context-sensitive.

q: Why is this kind of grammar called context-sensitive?
options: A variable may be rewritten only when the right symbols surround it (αAβ → αγβ)
It depends on the context of the programming language
Its rules are applied in a fixed order
explain: In the equivalent form αAβ → αγβ, the rewrite of A to γ depends on its neighbours α and β. A context-free rule rewrites A anywhere.

q: In the aⁿbⁿcⁿ grammar, how many rule applications does the derivation of aabbcc take?
explain: S ⇒ aSBC ⇒ aaBCBC ⇒ aaBBCC ⇒ aabBCC ⇒ aabbCC ⇒ aabbcC ⇒ aabbcc. That is 2 steps to lay down symbols, 1 swap and 4 terminal rewrites.
